title: What is latitude?
answer: Latitude tells you how far north or south a place is from Earth’s equator. Imagine putting a belt around the middle of a globe. That belt marks zero degrees of latitude. A place north of the belt has a north latitude, and a place south of it has a south latitude. Lines of equal latitude run around the globe like rings, getting smaller near the poles. Many places share one latitude. To find a single point, you also need its longitude.

title: What is longitude?
answer: Longitude tells you how far east or west a place is from the line chosen as zero longitude. This starting line is called the prime meridian. Longitude lines meet at the North and South poles. Picture the seams between slices of an orange going from its top to its bottom. If you only know a place’s longitude, it could be anywhere along one line. Put longitude together with latitude to give an address that works even in the middle of an ocean.

title: Where is the equator?
answer: The equator is an imaginary circle around Earth halfway between the North Pole and the South Pole. It divides Earth into the Northern Hemisphere and Southern Hemisphere. A hemisphere is half of a ball, so you can picture cutting a globe into two pieces along that line. The equator is the starting place for measuring latitude. If you crossed it by boat or on a road, you would normally need a map or a sign to know when you had passed from one side to the other.

title: Why do flat maps stretch Earth?
answer: The surface of Earth curves, but paper is flat. Any way of drawing that curved surface on a flat page changes something about the places on it. One map might show the sizes of countries clearly but bend or stretch their shapes. Another map might help someone follow a steady direction at sea but make land near the poles look much bigger than it is. A map projection is a method for making that flat picture. Mapmakers choose one that works for the task at hand.

title: What are the continents?
answer: Continents are Earth’s biggest regions of land. A common way to name them uses seven: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Australia, Europe, North America, and South America. The list is a way people organize the map. Europe and Asia, for example, share one large stretch of land. Some maps group the two together as Eurasia. Continents are much larger than most countries. Africa holds many countries, while a common school map uses the name Australia for both a country and the smallest continent.

title: Canada
answer: Canada covers a large part of North America, from the Atlantic Ocean in the east to the Pacific Ocean in the west and the Arctic Ocean to the north. A trip across it can take you through rocky mountains, broad plains, forests, and lakes. Its capital, Ottawa, is in the eastern part of the country, near the border between Ontario and Quebec. English and French are the two official languages of Canada’s federal government. Canada shares a land border with the United States.

title: United States
answer: The United States of America lies in North America and includes 50 states. Most form one connected group between Canada and Mexico. Alaska sits northwest of that group, with part of Canada between them. Hawaii is a group of islands in the Pacific Ocean. The national capital is Washington, D.C., which is a district rather than a state. The country’s landscapes include the Appalachian Mountains in the east, the Rocky Mountains in the west, and the Mississippi River between them.

title: Mexico
answer: Mexico is in North America, just south of the United States. The Pacific Ocean is on one side and the Gulf of Mexico is on the other. The country’s land changes a great deal as you travel. Parts of the north are dry, some central areas have tall mountains, and rain forests grow in warmer parts of the south. Mexico City, the country’s capital, is inland. You can hear mariachi, a kind of Mexican music often played by groups, at some celebrations.

title: Brazil
answer: Brazil is the largest country in South America by area. Its eastern edge is along the Atlantic Ocean. The Amazon River crosses the north, where a large part of the Amazon rain forest grows. Elsewhere Brazil has landscapes such as mountains and long stretches of coast. The capital is Brasília, a city inland, and Portuguese is the official language. If you look at a map of Brazil and look only for forest, you will miss the large cities and other kinds of land people call home.

title: Egypt
answer: Egypt is a country mostly in northeastern Africa. Much of its land is desert, while fields and cities lie along the Nile River. The river flows north into the Mediterranean Sea. Near the coast it splits into branches across a wide, low area called a delta. Cairo is the capital. Close to it are the stone pyramids and the Great Sphinx at Giza, built thousands of years ago. Egypt today is home to millions of people, as well as to these remains from the past.

title: India
answer: India is a country in southern Asia. The Himalayas rise along its north, and a large part of the country reaches south into the Indian Ocean region. Between those places you can find river plains, high land, and busy cities. The national capital is New Delhi. Many languages are used in India, so you may hear different words for the same thing when traveling from one area to another. The Ganges is one of India’s major rivers.

title: Japan
answer: Japan is a chain of islands off the eastern side of Asia. A group of islands is called an archipelago. Honshu is the largest island and the one with Tokyo, the capital. The other three main islands are Hokkaido, Shikoku, and Kyushu. Mountains cover much of the country, so many towns and cities grew on flatter land near the coasts. Mount Fuji, a volcano on Honshu, is Japan’s highest mountain.

title: Australia
answer: Australia is a country in the Southern Hemisphere. Much of the middle is dry. Many people live in cities nearer the coast, including Sydney. The capital is Canberra, inland from the east coast. Beyond the northeast coast lies the Great Barrier Reef, where corals have built places for other sea life to live. Australia’s animals include kangaroos and koalas, mammals whose young develop in a pouch. Tasmania, an island south of the mainland, is part of Australia too.

title: Kenya
answer: Kenya is in East Africa, and the equator runs across it. Its eastern coast meets the Indian Ocean. Farther inland are grasslands, hills, and high mountains. Nairobi is the capital. People use many languages in Kenya, including English and Swahili, its two official languages. Some places have been set aside as parks or reserves where animals such as elephants can live. Many people live in towns or cities and have daily lives very different from a trip through a wildlife park.

title: France
answer: Most of France’s land is in western Europe. Paris, its capital, grew along the Seine River. The city is home to the Eiffel Tower and the Arc de Triomphe. The Alps rise to the east and the Pyrenees run along part of the country’s border with Spain. France also includes places far from Europe, such as French Guiana in South America. French is the country’s official language. If you have seen a price in euros, you have seen the kind of money used in Paris.

title: How did people live in ancient Egypt?
answer: In ancient Egypt, much of daily life followed the Nile River. Flooding once left rich mud across nearby fields. People farmed that land and carried water to their crops in channels. They caught fish and used river plants to make a writing material called papyrus. Villages and cities depended on the work of farmers, builders, craft workers, and people who could read and write. Over thousands of years, Egyptian rulers and beliefs changed, so a family in one period could live differently from a family many centuries later.

title: Why was the Great Pyramid built?
answer: The Great Pyramid at Giza was built as a tomb for Khufu, a ruler of ancient Egypt. It rises from a broad, square base and has four sides that slope toward the top. Inside are stone passages and chambers. The pyramid is the largest of three famous pyramids at Giza. It stands near other structures that belonged to a royal burial site, including smaller pyramids and tombs. Egyptologists, people who study ancient Egypt, still ask exactly how builders moved and lifted all that stone.

title: How do Egyptian hieroglyphs work?
answer: Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs are signs used to write the Egyptian language. Some are easy to recognize as pictures, such as an owl or an eye. Their job still depends on where they appear in the writing. One sign can stand for a sound. Another can stand for a whole word. Some give a reader a clue about what kind of word appears nearby. A reader therefore needs to know the writing system to understand a line of signs, just as reading English takes more than recognizing a letter’s shape.

title: How did the Rosetta Stone help people read hieroglyphs?
answer: The Rosetta Stone has the same announcement carved in three kinds of writing. One is in Greek, which scholars could already read. The other two use ancient Egyptian scripts, called hieroglyphs and Demotic. Comparing the parts gave scholars clues to the Egyptian signs. A royal name, for example, could help them make a guess about which signs represented its sounds. The stone is only part of a larger slab. Much of its upper section is missing, so there were gaps to work around.

title: Why did people press signs into clay?
answer: In ancient Mesopotamia, people used clay tablets as writing surfaces. A writer used a tool called a stylus to press small wedge shapes into soft clay. Groups of wedges formed signs in a system called cuneiform. Keeping track of food and other goods was one early use. People also wrote letters, stories, and math on tablets. A clay tablet could dry and become hard, allowing some messages to last for thousands of years. The marks often survive even when part of the tablet breaks.

title: What was ancient Greece?
answer: Ancient Greece included many communities around the sea. Some cities and the area around each city formed a separate government. We call these places city-states. Athens and Sparta were two powerful examples. Many communities shared parts of their language and religion, and athletes traveled to meet at festivals. They could also disagree and fight wars. Objects such as painted pots and buildings with carved stone can show how people worked, played sports, and honored their gods.

title: What happened at the ancient Olympic Games?
answer: The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia in Greece as part of a festival honoring the god Zeus. Athletes competed in events such as running, wrestling, and chariot racing. The games took place every four years. The athletes who could enter were limited by rules that would seem unfair today. For example, the regular events were for male competitors, though a woman who owned the horses and chariot that won a race could receive the prize. You can still see places at Olympia where people gathered and competed.

title: Why did ancient Romans build so many roads?
answer: Roads tied ancient Rome to places across its growing territory. A good road made it easier to move travelers, soldiers, animals, and goods over land. One well-known example is the Appian Way, which started at Rome and was later extended to the port city of Brindisi. Parts were paved with stone. A road also needed structures such as bridges and places to get through steep land. Some sections of ancient roads remain visible today, giving us a look at how people traveled long before cars.

title: How did Roman aqueducts carry water?
answer: A Roman aqueduct carried water from a source, such as a spring, toward a place people needed it. Builders gave the water channel a gentle downhill slope so gravity kept the water moving. When the channel reached a valley, a bridge could hold it high enough to keep that slope. The stone arches you see in some pictures are supports. The water flowed in a channel near the top. Other parts of a long journey might run through a tunnel or along the ground.

title: What did the Declaration of Independence say?
answer: In 1776, the Continental Congress approved a document saying that 13 British colonies in North America were separating from Great Britain. The Declaration of Independence explained why they were taking that step and described rights they said people should have. The war with Britain was already underway. The ideas in the document went farther than what the new country put into practice at the time. For example, slavery continued even after the leaders said that people were equal.

title: What is the U.S. Constitution?
answer: The U.S. Constitution sets the basic rules for the United States government. It says what the different branches of the federal government may do and sets limits on their power. Delegates met in Philadelphia in 1787 to write it. Afterward, states held meetings to decide whether to approve it. The Constitution can be changed by adding amendments. A person trying to understand the rules today needs to look at the original document and the amendments together.

title: What are the three branches of the U.S. government?
answer: The United States divides federal government work among three branches. The legislative branch, Congress, makes federal laws. The executive branch, led by the president, carries out those laws. The judicial branch includes the federal courts, which decide cases and interpret laws. Each branch has some ways to check the power of another. A president can reject a bill passed by Congress, for example, but Congress can still pass it if enough lawmakers in both parts vote to override that decision.

title: What is the U.S. Congress?
answer: Congress is the part of the United States government that makes federal laws. It has two parts, called the House of Representatives and the Senate. Every state has two senators. States with more people usually have more seats in the House than states with fewer people. Members in both parts study problems, talk about ideas for laws, and vote. To send a bill to the president, the House and Senate generally must agree to the same words in it.

title: What is the U.S. Bill of Rights?
answer: The Bill of Rights is the name for the first ten amendments to the U.S. Constitution. An amendment adds to or changes a rule in the Constitution. The First Amendment protects freedoms that include religion, speech, and the right to gather peacefully. Other amendments set rules about searches and how people are treated in court. These protections put limits on government power. People sometimes disagree about how the words apply to a new situation, so courts may have to decide what the protections require.

title: How did the Nineteenth Amendment change voting?
answer: The Nineteenth Amendment says that a U.S. citizen’s right to vote cannot be denied because of their sex. In the years before 1920, some states already allowed women to vote in some or all elections, while others did not. After years of organizing and debate, enough states approved the amendment in 1920 for it to take effect across the country. People still faced other unfair barriers to voting. For instance, officials in some states continued to use racist rules and practices to turn Black citizens away.

title: What does federalism mean in the United States?
answer: Federalism means that governing power is divided between the national government and the states. The U.S. Constitution gives the national government powers such as making rules for trade across state borders. States have their own governments and make many of the rules people use close to home. For example, they issue driver’s licenses. Some responsibilities overlap, and both levels can collect taxes. The Constitution sets rules that help people decide which level of government may act when there is a disagreement.

title: Why does the United States take a census?
answer: A census counts the people who live in a place. The United States takes a census of the whole country once every ten years. One reason is to figure out how to divide seats in the House of Representatives among the states. Population changes can make a state gain or lose seats after a census. Census numbers also help communities plan. If many more children live in an area than before, for example, planners can use population information while thinking about schools and other services.

Archivists organize these records so people can find them, and they protect fragile pieces from damage so future readers can study them too.

title: How do people read braille?
answer: Braille uses patterns of raised dots. A reader feels them with their fingertips. In six-dot braille, each space, called a cell, has room for six dots arranged in two columns. Which dots stick up tells the reader what the pattern means. Braille can represent letters, numbers, and other signs. In some versions, one pattern can stand for a whole word or a group of letters to save space. People use braille to read books, label things, and find their way around buildings.

title: How does American Sign Language work?
answer: American Sign Language, or ASL, is a language that people can see. Signers use their hands, faces, and bodies to express ideas. A change in where or how a sign moves can matter, much as a change in sound can matter in a spoken language. ASL has its own grammar, the patterns people use to put ideas together. Some signs may look a little like what they mean, but people need to learn the language to understand a conversation.

title: What is an alphabet?
answer: An alphabet is a set of letters used to write a language. In an alphabet, letters or groups of letters stand for sounds. This gives a writer a way to spell many words with a small set of signs. English uses 26 letters. The spelling does not always tell you which sound to make. In the word ship, for instance, s and h together stand for one sound. Other writing systems organize signs differently, and languages using the same alphabet can give its letters different jobs.

title: How can you count syllables in a word?
answer: A syllable is one sound part of a spoken word. Say rainbow slowly and listen for two parts, rain and bow. If you clap once on each part, you clap twice. Frog has one syllable and dinosaur has three. A syllable usually has a vowel sound that you can hear, such as the long a sound in rain. Counting letters on the page will not tell you how many syllables you said. A word like cake has four letters but just one syllable.

title: What can a portrait tell us?
answer: A portrait is an artwork about a person or group of people. It could be a painting, a photograph, a drawing, or a sculpture. An artist can show more than a face. A runner holding a worn pair of shoes might suggest years of practice. A picture of someone at their kitchen table might tell a different story about the same person than a picture on a stage. Looking at choices such as the pose, clothes, and setting can help you see what the artist wanted you to notice.
aliases: why are objects in paintings of people
facts: The person shown in a portrait is sometimes called the subject or sitter.
When an artist makes a portrait of themself, it is called a self-portrait.

title: How does a woodcut make a picture?
answer: To make a woodcut, an artist carves away the parts of a flat block that should stay blank on the picture. The raised parts that are left get covered with ink. Press paper against them and the ink moves to the paper. You can see the same idea in a stamp, where only the raised parts make a mark. One carved block can print several pictures. The print faces the opposite way from the block, so a letter on the block must be reversed to read correctly on paper.
facts: A woodcut is a kind of relief printing.
Artists can print with different blocks to add different colors.

title: What goes on behind the scenes in a museum?
answer: A museum collects and cares for objects that can teach people something. A museum might hold paintings, historic clothing, fossils, or dried plants. Only part of a big collection fits in the rooms visitors can walk through. Staff also measure, photograph, label, and store objects so they can be found and studied later. A conservator helps protect fragile things. If a piece of cloth can fade in bright light, for example, a museum may show it only under dim light for part of the year.
facts: The objects a museum has gathered and cares for form its collection.
Researchers can study some objects that are kept in storage.

title: What is the Library of Congress?
answer: The Library of Congress is a research library in Washington, D.C. It helps people in Congress find information they need and also makes materials available to the public. Books are only part of what it keeps. Its collections include maps, photographs, sound recordings, and music. A catalog helps people look up what the library has and where to find it. The library also runs a service that makes books available in forms such as braille and audio for eligible readers.

title: How do orchestra musicians play together?
answer: An orchestra is a group of musicians who play different instruments together. A typical orchestra includes strings, woodwinds, brass, and percussion. The groups may play different parts at the same time. To line up their sounds, musicians follow written music and listen to each other. Many orchestras have a conductor who uses gestures to show when to start, how fast to play, or when to get quieter. The same group can make a tiny sound or fill a large room with music.

facts: Violins and cellos belong to the string family.

title: Is rhythm the same as the beat?
answer: The beat is the steady pulse you can tap along to in much music. Rhythm is the pattern made by sounds and silences as time goes by. Try tapping slowly and evenly with one hand while a partner says “I can run.” Your partner can bunch the syllables together or stretch them across more than one tap. In an orchestra or a band, one person can play quick sounds while another plays slow ones, and both can still fit into the same beat.
aliases: what is a beat in music
facts: A pause can be part of a rhythm.
A rhythm can put several short sounds in the time of one beat.

title: How do written notes tell us what to play?
answer: Written music gives performers a set of marks to follow. In a familiar kind of musical notation, notes sit on or between five lines called a staff. Moving a note higher on the staff usually shows that it should sound higher. The note’s shape can tell how long the player should hold it. A rest marks time when that player should be silent. People can learn and share many kinds of music by ear too. Written music is one way to keep a record that others can follow.

facts: A musical staff has five lines in common Western staff notation.

title: How did basketball begin?
answer: James Naismith invented basketball in Springfield, Massachusetts, in 1891. He was looking for a game people could play indoors in winter. The first players tried to toss a ball into peach baskets mounted above the floor. At first, the ball had to be taken back out of a basket after a score. The game changed over time. Players in modern basketball can bounce the ball to move with it, and the ball drops straight through an open net when a shot goes in.
facts: Naismith wrote 13 original rules.
In a standard game, each side has five players on the court at once.

title: What are volleyball players trying to do?
answer: Volleyball teams send a ball over a net and try to land it in the other team’s court. They can also score when the other team makes a mistake, such as hitting the ball out. In indoor volleyball, a team usually has as many as three touches to return the ball. Players often use one touch to receive it, a second to set it up in the air, and a third to strike it over the net. Players try to keep the ball moving without catching it.

sections.text: William G. Morgan invented volleyball in Holyoke, Massachusetts, in 1895. He first called it Mintonette.

title: How do you score in soccer?
answer: In soccer, two teams try to get the ball into the other team’s goal. A goal counts when the whole ball goes over the goal line between the posts and under the crossbar, as long as the scoring team has not broken a rule. Players usually move the ball with their feet, but may also play it with other parts of their body, such as their head. The goalkeeper can use their hands in their own penalty area, subject to rules other players do not have.
facts: Many countries call the game football.

title: How did the modern Olympic Games begin?
answer: The first modern Olympic Games opened in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Organizers drew inspiration from games held long before at Olympia. The modern event brought athletes from different countries together to compete. It has changed a great deal since then. There are now summer and winter editions, along with sports that were not in the first modern program. The city that welcomes the athletes can change from one edition to another, so the games are often held far from Greece.

facts: The International Olympic Committee was founded in 1894.
The first modern Winter Olympic Games were held in Chamonix, France, in 1924.

title: Where did corn come from?
answer: Corn, also called maize, grew into a farm crop from a wild plant called teosinte. This change began thousands of years ago in what is now Mexico. People saved seeds from plants they wanted to grow again. Over many generations, the plants changed a great deal, including the size and shape of the part that holds the kernels. Farmers in different regions grew many kinds of maize. Today, an ear of maize can look very different depending on which variety it is.

sections.heading: Tiny clues
sections.text: Researchers in Mexico found tiny traces of maize on ancient tools. Even when a whole cob has disappeared, those traces can help scientists find when people were using the crop.

facts: Maize was grown in the Americas long before it reached Europe.

title: Why do farmers change crops in a field?
answer: Crop rotation means planning to grow different crops in the same place at different times. If a disease can easily spread among one kind of plant, growing an unrelated plant in that field for a while can leave the disease with fewer plants to infect. Different crops can also give the soil different kinds of roots and cover. The plan depends on the land. For example, a gardener growing beans after tomatoes is using a different rotation from a big farm alternating corn and soybeans.
aliases: why do farmers plant different crops every year
facts: A crop rotation has a planned order that uses more than one kind of crop.
Rotation can help manage some plant diseases.

title: Why do people save seeds in seed banks?
answer: A seed bank stores seeds so people can grow their plants again in the future. It may hold many varieties of one crop. Some varieties have useful differences, such as growing better in a dry place. For many crops, keeping seeds dry and cold helps them stay alive for a long time. Staff test seeds to see which ones still sprout. When a supply gets too low, the seed bank can arrange to grow plants and gather fresh seeds.

sections.text: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault in Norway keeps backup seed collections that belong to institutions around the world.

title: How do farmers water crops when it does not rain?
answer: Irrigation means bringing water to a place where plants need it. A farm may get water from a river, a well, or a place where water has been stored. Sprinklers send water through the air. Other systems let water move along channels, or drip it near each plant’s roots. How much water a farmer uses depends on the soil, crop, weather, and other conditions. Irrigation can help crops grow when the ground is dry, but the water still has to come from a supply that can meet the farm’s needs.
facts: Drip irrigation releases water slowly near plants.
Irrigation water can come from below ground or from an above-ground source.

title: Why do people use money?
answer: Money makes it easier to buy and sell things. Imagine you make a hat and want a book. If the person with the book does not want a hat, you can sell your hat to someone else and use the money for the book. A common money unit also gives people a way to compare costs. A book priced at ten dollars costs twice as much as one priced at five dollars. People can also save money and use it for something later.
facts: Coins and paper bills are examples of money people can hold.
Merchants can list prices in a shared money unit such as dollars.

title: How does barter work?
answer: Barter means trading something directly for something else. You might trade a comic you have already read for a book a friend has finished. The two of you would each have something the other wants. But what if your friend has the book and wants a pencil instead? You would have to find a pencil or work out another trade. That is one reason people find it easier to trade many different things when everyone uses the same kind of money.
facts: People can offer to do a job as part of a barter trade.

title: What is a euro?
answer: The euro is a kind of money used in many European countries, including France. A euro is divided into 100 cents. If you travel between countries that use the euro, you can compare prices and spend euro coins in either place. Take a close look at a euro coin. One side has a design used in common, while the other side can have a design chosen by the country that issued the coin. Different designs can still have the same value.

title: Why was Yellowstone made a national park?
answer: Yellowstone became a national park in 1872. An important reason was that people wanted to keep its geysers, hot springs, and other unusual natural features protected and open to visitors. A geyser can send a burst of steam and water up from the ground. One famous geyser, Old Faithful, has drawn visitors for many years. Yellowstone also includes rivers, forests, and habitat for wildlife. Most of the park is in Wyoming, with parts in Montana and Idaho.

sections.heading: How to look
sections.text: At Yellowstone’s hot areas, visitors stay on boardwalks and other marked paths. Even ground that looks solid can be hot and unsafe.

facts: Yellowstone opened as the first U.S. national park.
